title: Evaluate PR 4: package-json version mode (commit-time version bump)
description:
PR 4 (branch claude/add-alternate-version-mode-Hnq9X) adds versionMode: "package-json" — a pre-commit hook that computes the next version and writes it into package.json, so the committed package.json always carries the real version. Goal (Justin): get the dynamic-version effect WITHOUT dynamic-version.local.json, which breaks CI (file is gitignored, remote envs must regenerate it) and breaks Expo EAS builds (which historically packed the repo without .git, making generation impossible). Target repos: eslint-config-jha-react-node, prompts — small, linear-history, low-ceremony.

Written ~2026-03 by Claude 4 Opus. Rebased onto main 2026-09-16 as local branch pr-4-package-json-mode (3 commits, one conflict in src/git-hooks-manager.ts resolved by keeping mains nonFatalSuffix and applying it to post-* hooks in both modes, deliberately NOT to pre-commit).
design:
VERDICT: the core idea is sound and worth keeping, but only for linear-history repos, and the implementation needs fixes before it is safe.

=== WHAT WORKS (verified by tests/integration/package-json-mode.test.ts, 16 tests) ===
- Sequential commits increment correctly in both calculation modes.
- Self-healing after --no-verify works exactly as designed: version set i commits ago yields +(i+1).
- The bumped version lands INSIDE the commit; working tree is left clean.
- package.json alone is sufficient for a consumer — no .git, no generated file. This is the goal of the PR and it is met.

=== VERIFIED BY TEST OR PROBE ===
1. npm STRIPS build metadata on publish. Probe: `npm publish --dry-run` on version 1.0.0+5 produced "publishprobe@1.0.0" and filename publishprobe-1.0.0.tgz. So append-commits — the DEFAULT calculation mode — makes every commit publish as the same version; the registry rejects the second. add-to-patch must be the default for this mode. (Closed as not-a-blocker in 70i.1: Justin does not publish to npm.)
2. Unequal-length branches ALWAYS conflict on package.json (test). Equal-length branches are subtler and worse: both sides compute the SAME version, git auto-merges cleanly, and the merged result undercounts (two commits of work, one version) (test). 70i.10 (branch suffix) makes that case a visible conflict.
3. The design-doc claim "on the merge commit the pre-commit hook recalculates" is FALSE (test). git merge fires pre-merge-commit, not pre-commit; auto-merge commits keep a stale version.
4. git commit --amend re-runs pre-commit and double-bumps (test).
5. Rebase never re-runs the hook: the branch gains a commit while the version stands still (test).
6. The hook reads/writes the WORKING TREE package.json then `git add`s the whole file, so an unstaged half-finished package.json edit is silently swept into the commit (test). Data integrity, not just a `git add -p` annoyance. Fixed by 70i.3.
7. updateLockfile() buys nothing. Probes: bun.lock records the root name but NOT the root version (grep: zero "version" keys), and `bun install --frozen-lockfile` after a version-only bump exits 0; package-lock.json DOES record the root version but `npm ci` after a version-only bump also exits 0. `npm version X --no-git-tag-version --offline` updates both files instantly and offline if the drift is ever worth closing. Removed by 70i.5.
8. A failing package manager inside the hook is swallowed: a stub npm that exits 1 (proven invoked via a marker file) leaves the commit succeeding with no signal (test). "Failure is not empty" violation. Fixed by 70i.4.

=== INFERRED FROM CODE READING, NOT DEMONSTRATED ===
9. stageFiles() also catches everything and only console.warn()s. If `git add` itself failed, package.json would be rewritten on disk but never staged, so the commit would record the OLD version while the tree shows the new one. I did not induce a git-add failure; this is a read of src/script-manager.ts, not an observation.
10. installCommand() calls generateVersionFile() (which creates version-manager.json with the default dynamic-file) BEFORE getVersionMode(), and no --mode flag exists — so a first install appears unable to produce package-json hooks; the user must install, hand-edit config, install again. Read from src/index.ts ordering; not executed end-to-end. (70i.7, not in the current push.)
11. installGitHooks() only writes the current mode's hooks and has no removal path, so switching package-json -> dynamic-file appears to leave pre-commit live forever. The leftover-file half IS covered by a test; that the leftover hook keeps bumping on later commits is inferred. (70i.6, not in the current push.)
12. RESERVED_VERSION_NAMES gains "main" with no rationale anywhere in the diff or the plan. Observation, not a defect.

=== STYLE / RULES ===
- docs/plans/2026-03-27_committed-version-modes.md violated the current critical rules (beads replaced docs/plans/). DONE 2026-09-19 (70i.9): deleted in 35987e0; content preserved above.
- calculatePreCommitVersion() duplicates its add-to-patch arithmetic three times.
- preCommitHandler(outputPath: string) is typed string but yargs supplies undefined (--output has no default); the ?? fallback is load-bearing while the type says it cannot fire.

=== CONDUCTOR DECISIONS, 2026-09-19 (binding on every dispatch in this push) ===

D1. SCOPE OF THIS PUSH. 70i.10, then 70i.2, 70i.3, 70i.5+70i.4, then 70i.8 if budget allows. 70i.6 and 70i.7 are explicitly NOT in this push. 70i.9 is done.

D2. BRANCH SUFFIX FORMAT (70i.10). `<core>-<sanitised-branch>.<n>` with the prerelease inserted before any +build metadata. Examples: 0.32.3 -> 0.32.3-feat-x.3; 0.32.1+3 -> 0.32.1-feat-x.3+3. A hyphen prerelease sorts BEFORE the release, which is correct: a branch build is a prerelease of the version it will become.

D3. VERSION-MANAGER OWNS THE PRERELEASE SEGMENT WHEN THE KNOB IS ON. This is the load-bearing decision. In package-json mode the decorated version is COMMITTED into package.json, so the next computation reads it back as its own input — a feedback loop that would otherwise compound (0.1.0-b.1 -> 0.1.0-b.1-b.2). Therefore: every computation strips the entire existing prerelease from the current/base version before calculating, and re-applies a freshly computed suffix at the end. Consequence, accepted and documented: with the knob ON, a hand-authored prerelease in package.json (1.0.0-beta.1) is discarded on the next hooked commit. The knob is off by default; this limitation is documented in the README and pinned by a test. REJECTED ALTERNATIVE: a marker token (0.32.1-branch.feat-x.3) that makes the suffix recognisable so hand-authored prereleases survive — rejected because it deviates from the shape Justin wrote down and buys a case he does not have. Revisit only if a real base prerelease appears.

D4. SANITISATION, exact rules. (a) Replace every character outside [0-9A-Za-z-] with '-' (so slashes AND dots in branch names both become '-'; the only dot in the suffix is the one before n). (b) Collapse runs of '-' to one. (c) Trim leading/trailing '-'. (d) Empty result -> the literal 'branch'. (e) All-digits result -> prefix 'b' (semver forbids leading zeros in a numeric identifier; 007 -> b007). Sanitisation is lossy and may collide (feat/x and feat-x both -> feat-x); that is accepted and documented.

D5. WHAT n IS. n = commits on this branch since its merge base with the main branch, measured by `git rev-list --count <mainBranch>..HEAD`, plus 1 in the pre-commit path for the about-to-happen commit. Reason: the count the modes already compute is useless here — in package-json mode the version changes on EVERY commit, so commitsSinceLastChange is always 0 and n would always be 1. If no configured main branch ref resolves, fall back to `git rev-list --count HEAD` (total commits) and say so in verbose output. If BOTH measurements fail, apply NO suffix and return the undecorated version — never substitute 0 for a failed measurement (critical rule 6).

D6. WHICH BRANCHES ARE "MAIN". config.branchSuffix.mainBranches, default ["main", "master"]. On a listed branch, and in detached HEAD (getCurrentBranch returns "HEAD"), no suffix is applied.

D7. n === 0 MEANS NO SUFFIX. A branch with no commits of its own is bit-identical to its base, so it gets the undecorated version. Prevents 0.32.1-my-branch.0 sorting below the release it equals.

D8. THE KNOB APPLIES TO BOTH versionModes. dynamic-file gets it in the generated file (no feedback hazard, base always comes from an undecorated package.json); package-json gets it committed. Same config field, same helper, one code path.

D9. INDEX IS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH IN PRE-COMMIT (70i.3). The current version is read from the INDEX (`git show :package.json`), which equals HEAD's content when package.json is unstaged — one rule covers both cases. The new content is written to the index surgically (hash-object + update-index), and the working-tree file gets only its version field rewritten, so unstaged edits elsewhere in package.json survive and are NOT staged.

D10. FAIL LOUDLY IN THE HOOK (70i.4). A failed stage or a failed package-manager call aborts the commit with a non-zero exit and a message naming the exact failed command. A commit that records the wrong version is worse than a blocked commit, and `--no-verify` self-heals by design.

D11. MERGE DRIVER POLICY (70i.8). Justin, 2026-09-19: default to OURS (the branch being merged into, i.e. main) for the version field. The pre-commit hook then adds exactly 1 on top, so a squash of a 500-commit branch lands at main+1.

D12. NO NEW dynamic-version.local.json IN package-json MODE (70i.2). In package-json mode nothing is written unless --output is passed explicitly; the post-* hooks are not installed, and the *.local.json gitignore prompt is skipped. The watcher and the metro plugin still write the file in package-json mode — out of scope here, filed as 70i.11.
acceptance_criteria: Justin has: (a) a clear verdict on whether the approach is worth keeping, (b) verified evidence for each claim rather than inference, (c) a prioritised list of what must change before it is safe to use, (d) automated tests that pin the behaviour so a future fix flips a documented expectation.
notes:
Test baseline MEASURED 2026-09-19 on a clean clone of main (fd700e5) and on pr-4-package-json-mode, full suite both sides: main 86 pass / 1 skip / 8 fail; branch 122 pass / 1 skip / 8 fail. IDENTICAL failing set, so the branch adds zero regressions and 36 passing tests:
  formatVersionOutput > compact mode > renders single line with version, branch, and checkmark
  formatVersionOutput > compact mode > shows dirty indicator when dirty

The earlier '7 pre-existing failures' figure was one short: the husky bun.lock failure is pre-existing on main too (verified by running that file against the main clone).

title: Default to add-to-patch in package-json mode (npm strips +N on publish)
notes: Closed 2026-09-16: Justin said "I do not currently publish almost anything to npm, so npm publish does not have to be a blocker." The finding stands (npm strips +N on publish, verified by npm publish --dry-run) but it is not a reason to change the default for him. If the branch-suffix idea (70i.10) lands, prerelease identifiers survive publish anyway, which makes this moot from a second direction.

title: Branch-name suffix in version when not on main (0.32.1-my-branch.3)
description:
Justin's idea (2026-09-16): when not on the main branch, include the branch name in the computed version, e.g. 0.32.1-my-branch.3.

STATUS 2026-09-19: BUILT AND VERIFIED on branch pr-4-package-json-mode. Commits cadafeb (source), 81de36f (tests), 07dcaa6 (README), 68ed093 (all-digits test). Not closed — awaiting conductor review.

WHAT EXISTS NOW
- src/branch-suffix.ts — pure, no I/O: sanitizeBranchName (D4), stripPrerelease, applyBranchSuffix (D2), isSuffixExemptBranch (D6), decideBranchSuffix (the D5/D6/D7 policy, taking measurements as input so every failure combination is unit-testable).
- src/git-utils.ts — countCommitsSinceRef(ref) and countCommitsOnHead(), both number | null, null on failure, never 0. countCommitsSinceRef refuses a ref outside /^[A-Za-z0-9._\/-]+$/ (it comes from user-authored config and reaches a shell).
- src/types.ts — BranchSuffixConfigSchema exactly as specified: enabled default false, mainBranches default [main, master], the whole object defaulted. Survives an absent field and a partial object; both are pinned by tests.
- src/version-generator.ts — measureBranchCommitCounts() + planBranchSuffix() + decorateVersion(); wired into BOTH generateFileBasedVersion() and generatePreCommitVersionData() (D8). GenerateVersionResult gained branchSuffixWarning: string | null.
- src/script-manager.ts — readPreCommitBaseVersion() / writePreCommitVersion(): the two named helpers 70i.3 swaps to index reads/writes. The suffix logic is not inlined into either.
- src/index.ts — preCommitHandler uses writePreCommitVersion; both handlers console.warn the branchSuffixWarning when the format is not silent.
- README.md — "Branch Name Suffix (opt-in)" section: format, n, sanitisation, precedence, and the D3 limitation.

D3 IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART. While the knob is on, the prerelease is stripped before either calculate function sees the version and a fresh suffix is applied after. Proven necessary, not assumed: with the strip removed, add-to-patch went 0.1.1-feat-x.1 -> 0.1.1-feat-x.2 -> 0.1.1-feat-x.3 — the CORE FROZE at 0.1.1 while only n advanced, silently, exit code 0.

SEMANTIC CONTRACTS (unchanged from the spec, all pinned by tests)
- Format <core>-<sanitised-branch>.<n>, prerelease before any +build metadata.
- n = commits since the merge base with the first main branch that resolves, +1 in pre-commit.
- Configured main branches and detached HEAD get no suffix.
- n === 0 gets no suffix.
- A failed measurement yields the UNDECORATED version, never n = 0 or n = 1.

OUT OF SCOPE AND UNTOUCHED: the merge driver (70i.8), the --mode flag (70i.7), stale-hook removal (70i.6), dropping dynamic-version.local.json writes (70i.2), the watcher/metro plugin (70i.11). The watcher and metro plugin DO inherit the knob, because they call generateFileBasedVersion; that is the shared-code-path consequence the spec allowed.
design:
DESIGN DECISIONS ARE IN THE EPIC (version-manager-70i) design field, items D2 through D8. Read them before starting; they are binding. Summary:
- Format <core>-<sanitised-branch>.<n>, prerelease inserted before any +build metadata (D2).
- version-manager OWNS the prerelease segment while the knob is on; strip before calculating, re-apply after (D3). This is the decision that prevents the feedback loop.
- Exact sanitisation rules (D4).
- n = commits since the merge base with the main branch, +1 in pre-commit; fallbacks and the no-measurement case (D5).
- mainBranches config, detached HEAD excluded (D6).
- n === 0 means no suffix (D7).
- Applies to both versionModes through one code path (D8).
acceptance_criteria:
GATE. `bun run signal` clean, and `bun test` showing no failure that main does not also have (measured baseline is recorded in the epic notes). Run the suite with npm_config_cache redirected into $TMPDIR or the install tests EPERM. New tests in this file get an explicit per-test timeout (>= 20000ms); the default 5s timeout makes package-json-mode tests flake under full-suite load.

BEHAVIOUR (each item needs a test)
1. Off by default. A config with no branchSuffix field, and a repo with no version-manager.json at all, both produce today's undecorated versions in both versionModes.
2. Sanitisation: branch "claude/add-alternate-version-mode-Hnq9X" produces a valid semver; so do branch names containing dots, spaces, and consecutive separators. Assert validity with semver.valid() from the `semver` package added as a DEV dependency only (runtime dep count stays where CLAUDE.md wants it), not with a hand-rolled regex.
3. Sanitisation edge cases: an all-punctuation branch name yields the literal "branch"; an all-digits branch name is prefixed with "b" (leading zeros are illegal in a semver numeric identifier).
4. main is untouched: on "main" and on "master" the version is undecorated with the knob ON. Detached HEAD (getCurrentBranch() returns "HEAD") is also undecorated.
5. n === 0 yields no suffix.
6. Equal-length branches no longer collide: the existing package-json-mode test that shows two equal-length branches auto-merging to the same undercounted version stays as the knob-OFF control, and a knob-ON twin shows the two sides producing DIFFERENT versions so the merge conflicts visibly instead of silently undercounting.
7. No feedback loop in package-json mode: with the knob on, successive commits on a branch go 0.1.1-feat-x.1 -> 0.1.2-feat-x.2 (add-to-patch) rather than compounding suffixes or freezing. Cover append-commits too: the prerelease sits before the +N metadata.
8. Both versionModes: dynamic-file writes the decorated version into dynamic-version.local.json; package-json commits it into package.json.
9. Failure is not empty: when the configured main branches do not resolve, the count falls back to the total commit count and the version is still produced; when no count can be measured at all, the UNDECORATED version is returned. No path may substitute 0 for a failed measurement.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS (required, and reported)
For at least the sanitisation test, the main-untouched test, and the feedback-loop test: break the implementation, watch the test fail, restore it, and report what the failure message was. An unproven test is no test.
notes:
GATE, measured 2026-09-19 on pr-4-package-json-mode at 68ed093.
- bun run signal: FULLY GREEN (ts-check, eslint, prettier).
- Full suite (TMPDIR=... npm_config_cache="$TMPDIR/npm-cache" bun test): 208 pass / 1 skip / 8 fail. The failing SET is byte-identical to the recorded baseline (2 compact-mode snapshots, 5 Watch Command, 1 husky bun.lock). NO ninth failure. Branch went 122 -> 208 passing, i.e. 86 new tests.
- New tests: 63 unit (tests/unit/branch-suffix.test.ts), 18 integration (tests/integration/branch-suffix.test.ts), 5 integration added to tests/integration/package-json-mode.test.ts. Every new integration test carries an explicit 30000ms timeout.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS RUN (break it, watch it fail, restore it)
1. Sanitisation — removed the character-class replace in sanitizeBranchName. 24 of 63 unit tests failed, e.g. Expected "claude-add-alternate-version-mode-Hnq9X" / Received "claude/add-alternate-version-mode-Hnq9X"; the semver-validity assertions failed with Received: null. Integration: Expected "0.32.2-claude-add-alternate-version-mode-Hnq9X.1" / Received "0.32.2-claude/add-alternate-version-mode-Hnq9X.1". Restored: 63/63 and 18/18.
2. Main-untouched — made isSuffixExemptBranch always return false. All three AC-4 tests failed: "0.1.2" vs "0.1.2-master.2", "0.1.2" vs "0.1.2-main.2", "0.1.2" vs "0.1.2-HEAD.2". The sibling control ("a non-main branch IS decorated") kept passing, so the three are not passing via D7. Restored: green.
3. Feedback loop — removed the D3 strip in generatePreCommitVersionData. add-to-patch produced ["0.1.1-feat-x.1", "0.1.1-feat-x.2", "0.1.1-feat-x.3"] instead of 0.1.1/0.1.2/0.1.3 — THE CORE FROZE, exit code 0, no error. The land-on-main test gave Expected "0.1.2" / Received "0.1.1-feat-x.1", frozen forever. Restored: green.
   NOTE from control 3: the append-commits path did NOT fail, because applyBranchSuffix strips internally and masked the missing strip. Only add-to-patch exposes it. So the defensive strip inside applyBranchSuffix is load-bearing for coverage, not decoration.

MEASUREMENTS MADE THIS SESSION
- git init.defaultBranch is "main" globally, so fixtures start on main; tests assert the base branch is main or master rather than assuming.
- semver.valid() returns the NORMALISED version, which DROPS build metadata. So valid("0.32.1-x.3+7") === "0.32.1-x.3". Assertions on +N cases check parseability plus the emitted string separately.
- In package-json mode commitsSinceLastChange is always 0, as the epic states (confirmed by the observed 1-per-commit increments).
- bun add EPERMs in the sandbox unless TMPDIR is pointed at a writable dir: TMPDIR=/tmp/claude-501/bun-tmp BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR=... bun add -d ... works.

DEVIATIONS FROM SPEC (all reported to the conductor)
D1. The git counting helper is TWO functions (countCommitsSinceRef, countCommitsOnHead), each number | null as specified, rather than one; the main-branch fallback loop lives in version-generator.measureBranchCommitCounts(). Reason: the spec also requires the fallback chain to be testable, and a pure decision function taking grouped measurements makes the "both measurements failed" branch unit-testable, which no integration fixture can reach.
D2. Integration tests live in a NEW file tests/integration/branch-suffix.test.ts, not only in package-json-mode.test.ts. Reason: the knob spans both version modes and that file is scoped to one. The AC-6 knob-ON twin IS in package-json-mode.test.ts, directly beneath the knob-OFF control it twins, as specified.
D3. @types/semver was added as a devDependency alongside semver. semver 7 ships no types and ts-check would fail without it. Neither is a runtime dependency.
D4. VersionManagerConfig now has branchSuffix as a REQUIRED output field (the schema default makes it so), which means any config version-manager REWRITES — a legacy migration, or a bump that updates custom versions — will now gain a branchSuffix block on disk. Configs that are merely read are untouched (the "does not modify new format config" test still passes). This falls out of the exact schema shape the epic specified; flagging it because it is user-visible.
D5. applyBranchSuffix() strips any existing prerelease internally, making it idempotent, and returns the undecorated version for n <= 0 or a non-integer n. The spec described it only as "inserts after the version core"; the guards are defensive.

NOT VERIFIED / KNOWN GAPS
- "No count can be measured at all" (AC 9, second half) is proven by UNIT test on decideBranchSuffix, not end to end. A repo where both git rev-list calls fail is a repo with no commits, and generateFileBasedVersion throws earlier at getGitDescribe, so no integration fixture can reach that branch.
- The all-punctuation branch name (AC 3) is unit-only: git will not create a branch whose name sanitises to nothing.
- The warning text is asserted end to end via "2>&1" appended to the CLI command, because TestRepo.runCli cannot return stderr on a SUCCESSFUL run (execSync returns stdout only). Left alone rather than rewriting a shared helper.
- The knob was deliberately NOT enabled in this repo own version-manager.json.
close_reason: Built and verified. Conductor re-ran the full suite independently rather than trusting the report: 208 pass / 1 skip / 8 fail, the failing set byte-identical to main's 8, so 86 net-new passing tests and no regression. bun run signal green. Code reviewed line by line: the D3 strip is applied in both computation paths AND on exempt branches (necessary — a decorated version that lands on main by fast-forward would otherwise freeze there), the two git measurements are grouped so a null can never read as a measured 0, mainBranches is shell-guarded before interpolation, and the 70i.3 seam (readPreCommitBaseVersion / writePreCommitVersion) is in place with no suffix logic inside it. Negative controls were run and their failure messages reported; control 3 showed the version core freezing at 0.1.1 with exit code 0, demonstrating the silent-freeze landmine rather than assuming it. Three interpretations of D3/D5 APPROVED as built. Two minor findings carried to the fix round in the findings bead, neither blocking. One out-of-scope change (an unrelated justin-sdk pin bump) was reverted by the conductor in a separate commit.

title: Watcher and metro plugin still write dynamic-version.local.json in package-json mode
description:
70i.2 stops the CLI and the git hooks from writing dynamic-version.local.json in package-json mode. src/watcher.ts and src/metro-plugin.ts were deliberately left out of that change and still write the file on every trigger, which reopens exactly the hole package-json mode exists to close.

FIX SHAPE: both call into the same generate path; make them respect the same mode decision 70i.2 centralises. A watcher running in package-json mode has nothing useful to write, so it should either no-op with one clear message at startup or refuse to start.
acceptance_criteria: A watcher run and a metro bundle in package-json mode both leave no dynamic-version.local.json, proven by a test. dynamic-file behaviour unchanged.

title: README documents nothing about package-json mode
description:
grep of README.md (442 lines) for versionMode, 'package-json mode' and 'package-json' returns ZERO hits. PR 4 shipped an entire second version mode with no user-facing documentation, and this push is adding a branch-suffix knob, a merge driver and several behaviour changes on top of it.

WHAT THE SECTION MUST COVER
- What package-json mode is and the problem it solves: the committed package.json carries the real version, so a consumer needs neither .git nor a generated file. Names the two failures that motivated it (CI regeneration, Expo EAS packing without .git).
- How to turn it on, exactly, including the fact that a fresh install currently cannot reach it without hand-editing version-manager.json (70i.7, still open).
- The branchSuffix knob: format, default (off), sanitisation rules, and the documented limitation that version-manager owns the prerelease segment while it is on.
- The merge driver, its ours policy, and honestly whether it works for merges done with GitHub's web buttons.
- KNOWN LIMITATIONS, stated plainly rather than buried: linear history only; git commit --amend double-bumps; rebase never re-runs the hook; auto-merge commits keep a stale version because git fires pre-merge-commit, not pre-commit. All four are measured, not guessed.

Do this LAST in the push, once the behaviour it describes has stopped moving.
acceptance_criteria: A README section documents package-json mode end to end: purpose, how to enable, the branchSuffix knob (format, default, sanitisation, prerelease-ownership limitation), the merge driver and its ours policy, and the four measured limitations (linear history only, amend double-bumps, rebase does not re-run the hook, auto-merge keeps a stale version). Every claim in it is one that a test in this repo pins or that the epic records as measured. `bun run signal` stays clean (prettier formats markdown).

title: Fix round: conductor review findings for the 70i push
description:
Running list of findings from conductor review between dispatches. Each is numbered, carries its fix shape, and is dispositioned when fixed. None of these blocked the dispatch that followed them.

F1 (from 70i.10, minor). countCommitsSinceRef() in src/git-utils.ts returns null for THREE different reasons — the ref failed SAFE_REF_PATTERN, the ref did not resolve, or git errored — and the caller's warning text then says 'none of the configured main branches resolved', which misattributes the first case. A user who writes a ref with an unusual character gets a message that sends them looking in the wrong place.
FIX SHAPE: return a discriminated result (or take the rejected-shape check out to the caller) so the warning can name the actual cause. Keep null meaning 'no measurement' at the decision boundary.

F2 (from 70i.10, minor, player-raised). TestRepo.runCli() uses execSync and so cannot return stderr on a SUCCESSFUL run, which forced the branch-suffix warning test to append '2>&1' to the command string. That works but it is a harness hack sitting in a test that asserts user-facing text.
FIX SHAPE: switch runCli to spawnSync and return {stdout, stderr, exitCode}, then drop the 2>&1. It is a shared helper used by every integration test, so change it deliberately and run the whole suite.

F3 (from 70i.10, accepted, not a defect — recorded so it is not rediscovered). Because branchSuffix carries a zod .default(), it is a REQUIRED field on the parsed config, so any version-manager.json that version-manager rewrites (a legacy migration, or a bump that updates custom versions) gains a branchSuffix block it did not have. Configs that are only read are untouched. This is a consequence of the schema shape the conductor specified, it makes the knob discoverable, and a test pins that read-only configs are not modified. No action unless Justin dislikes it.
acceptance_criteria: Every numbered finding is either fixed with a test, or explicitly dispositioned in this bead as accepted-with-reason. `bun run signal` clean and no failure main does not also have.

title: install --silent adds no package.json scripts
description:
installCommand() in src/index.ts puts the ENTIRE script-installation block inside `if (!silent)`, together with the console output it was presumably meant to guard. So `version-manager install --silent` installs git hooks and then adds none of the dynamic-version scripts (dynamic-version, :install, :install-scripts, :generate, plus prepare/prebuild/predev/prestart in dynamic-file mode), without saying so.

VERIFIED 2026-09-19 by probe, not inferred: a temp repo in dynamic-file mode with husky pre-declared, run with `install --silent --non-interactive`, came out with hooks installed and package.json carrying no scripts key at all.

Pre-existing on main and unrelated to version-manager-70i.2, which only ran into it because its install tests had to drop --silent in order to observe the scripts at all.

FIX SHAPE: hoist the script installation out of the `if (!silent)` block and leave only its console.log() calls inside.
acceptance_criteria: `install --silent` adds the same scripts a non-silent install adds, and prints nothing — proven by a test asserting both the scripts in package.json and empty stdout. Non-silent install behaviour unchanged.

title: A pre-70i.2 dynamic-version.local.json is left behind and goes stale
description:
version-manager-70i.2 stops package-json mode from WRITING dynamic-version.local.json, but nothing removes one that an earlier version already wrote. A repo that upgrades keeps the old file on disk, and from then on it is never updated: anything importing it reads a version frozen at the moment of the upgrade, with no signal that it has stopped tracking.

That is worse than the file being absent — absent fails loudly at the import, stale reads as current.

Deliberately NOT fixed in 70i.2: deleting a user's file is not something that change should do unasked. Sibling of version-manager-70i.6 (remove stale HOOKS when versionMode changes); both are "clean up what an earlier install left behind" and could land together.

FIX SHAPE: on `install` in package-json mode, detect an existing generated file and either delete it after saying so, or refuse to touch it and print a one-line warning naming the path. Do not delete silently.
acceptance_criteria: After upgrading a package-json-mode repo that already has a dynamic-version.local.json, the user is told about the stale file (or it is removed with an explicit message), proven by a test. Nothing is deleted silently, and dynamic-file mode is unaffected.

title: Stop writing dynamic-version.local.json in package-json mode
description:
THE POINT OF THE WHOLE PR, AND IT IS BUILT. Justin's goal for package-json mode: the dynamic-version effect WITHOUT dynamic-version.local.json, because that file is gitignored — CI must regenerate it (which needs .git) and Expo EAS builds historically packed the repo without .git. PR 4 added the commit-time bump but left every generated-file path in place, so the mode did both. This bead removed the second half.

WHAT LANDED (branch pr-4-package-json-mode)
- 5af80ec feat: the behaviour change.
- f66f6a6 test: the tests.

THE DESIGN. src/generated-file-policy.ts is the single place that decides whether anything is written. Both the CLI path (generateVersionFile) and the hook path (preCommitHandler) in src/index.ts call writeGeneratedFiles(), so the two cannot drift apart. The rule: dynamic-file mode always writes; package-json mode writes only when --output was passed explicitly.

HOW EXPLICITNESS IS KNOWN. The --output option no longer declares a yargs default; resolveOutputPathOption() applies DEFAULT_OUTPUT_PATH and records explicit true/false. Provenance cannot be recovered by comparing the value against the default string — "--output ./dynamic-version.local.json" and no flag at all produce the same string — so the yargs default was removed rather than compared against. defaultDescription keeps --help showing the default (the only visible difference: the path is no longer quoted in the help line).

WHAT ELSE STOPPED IN package-json MODE
- No post-checkout / post-merge / post-rewrite hooks. Their only job was regenerating the file. (post-commit was already absent: pre-commit covers the commit.) PACKAGE_JSON_MODE_POST_HOOKS is deleted from src/git-hooks-manager.ts.
- No prepare/prebuild/predev/prestart lifecycle scripts: addScriptsToPackageJson()'s existing includeLifecycleScripts parameter is now driven by the mode. The bead named prebuild/predev/prestart; "prepare" is in the same LIFECYCLE_SCRIPTS list and has the same sole purpose ("Generate version file after npm install (for CI)"), so it goes too.
- No *.local.json gitignore prompt. Gated on "will THIS run write a file" (mode + explicit --output), while hooks and lifecycle scripts are gated on the mode alone, since neither ever passes --output.
- No dynamic-version.local.d.ts: it is written by the same gated call.

OUTPUT HONESTY. VersionOutputData.outputPath is now string | null; null drops the "save" lines and the compact disk marker, so the CLI cannot report a save that did not happen. generateTypeDefinitions() now returns the .d.ts path it wrote, so that name is derived in one place instead of three.

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE
- The watcher and the metro plugin still write the file in package-json mode: version-manager-70i.11, untouched here.
- Hooks/scripts left behind by an EARLIER install are not removed: version-manager-70i.6.
- A dynamic-version.local.json left behind by an earlier install is not removed either, and now goes stale: filed as version-manager-70i.15.
- bump still prints "Regenerating dynamic-version.local.json..." before calling the generate path, which in package-json mode now writes nothing. Left alone rather than reworded, because the line is shared with dynamic-file mode and this bead must not change dynamic-file output. Conductor's call.
- README/CLAUDE.md say nothing about any of this: version-manager-70i.12.
acceptance_criteria:
GATE. `bun run signal` clean. `bun test` with no failure main does not also have (baseline in the epic notes); run with npm_config_cache redirected into $TMPDIR or the install tests EPERM. New integration tests get an explicit per-test timeout of at least 20000ms.

BEHAVIOUR (each item needs a test)
1. In package-json mode, a hooked commit leaves NO dynamic-version.local.json and NO dynamic-version.local.d.ts anywhere in the repo, while package.json carries the bumped version.
2. In package-json mode, running the generate command with no flags writes no file and still prints the computed version to stdout.
3. In package-json mode, running the generate command with an explicit --output PATH writes that file.
4. In package-json mode, install writes a pre-commit hook and NO post-* version-manager lines at all. Verified starting point: src/git-hooks-manager.ts already omits post-commit in this mode (pre-commit covers it) but still writes PACKAGE_JSON_MODE_POST_HOOKS = post-checkout, post-merge, post-rewrite, whose only job is regenerating the file. Those three are what this bead removes.
5. In package-json mode, install does not add the generated-file lifecycle scripts and does not prompt about *.local.json in .gitignore.
6. Regression: in dynamic-file mode all four post-* hooks, the lifecycle scripts, the gitignore prompt and the generated file behave exactly as before. The existing dynamic-file tests must pass unmodified — if a test needs changing, that is a signal the change leaked.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS (required, and reported)
For items 1 and 6: break the implementation, watch the test fail, restore it, report the failure message.
notes:
VERIFICATION, 2026-09-19 (recipe: TMPDIR="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}" npm_config_cache="$TMPDIR/npm-cache" bun test).

GATE. bun run signal fully green. Full suite BEFORE the change, measured in this session: 208 pass / 1 skip / 8 fail. AFTER: 222 pass / 1 skip / 8 fail, the SAME eight — two stale compact-format snapshots, five Watch Command tests, one husky bun.lock test. No ninth failure; +14 tests.

NOT VERIFIED. No test drives the watcher or metro plugin in package-json mode (70i.11 owns that). No test covers an explicit --output reaching the PRE-COMMIT path, because the installed hook never passes --output; the shared writeGeneratedFiles() call is the argument that it would behave the same, which is construction, not observation.

FOUND WHILE HERE: version-manager-70i.14 (install --silent adds no scripts at all, pre-existing, verified by probe) and version-manager-70i.15 (a pre-existing generated file is left behind and goes stale).

title: Pre-commit hook must read the INDEX, not the working tree
description:
DATA INTEGRITY BUG, demonstrated by a test already on this branch. The pre-commit hook reads the WORKING TREE package.json, rewrites its version, then runs `git add package.json` on the whole file. Any unstaged edit sitting in package.json — a half-added dependency, a script being drafted — is silently swept into a commit the author never staged it for. This is not a `git add -p` annoyance; it puts content into history that the author did not choose to commit.

THE CONTRACT (epic design D9)
- The CURRENT version is read from the INDEX: `git show :package.json`. When package.json is unstaged this returns HEAD's content, so one rule covers both the staged and the unstaged case with no branching.
- The NEW index content is the index content with ONLY the version value replaced. Write it with `git hash-object -w --stdin` followed by `git update-index --cacheinfo 100644,<sha>,package.json`, so nothing else about the index moves.
- The WORKING TREE file gets only its version value rewritten, as a STRING-LEVEL replacement on the working-tree bytes. Do NOT parse and re-stringify: the whole point is to preserve a half-edited file, and a reformat destroys it. Unstaged edits elsewhere in the file survive and stay unstaged.
- If package.json is absent from the index (a brand-new repo with nothing committed), fall back to the working tree and say so in verbose output.

IN SCOPE
- The read and write helpers in the pre-commit path (70i.10 isolates them; swap their bodies).
- A git-utils helper to read a path's blob from the index, returning string | null — null strictly means "not in the index", never "read failed". A read failure must surface as a thrown error (critical rule 6).
- Keep the existing behaviour that the version DOES land in the commit even when the author staged nothing in package.json. That is the mode's purpose, not a bug.

OUT OF SCOPE
- Failing loudly when staging fails (70i.4) — that is the next bead and touches the same call site. Do not pre-empt it.
- Anything about merges, amend or rebase (70i.8).

NOTE, measured: this does NOT change any merge outcome recorded in 70i.8. In both merge flows the resolved version is already STAGED, so reading the index yields exactly what reading the working tree yielded.
acceptance_criteria:
GATE. `bun run signal` clean. `bun test` with no failure main does not also have (baseline in the epic notes); npm_config_cache redirected into $TMPDIR. New integration tests carry an explicit per-test timeout of at least 20000ms.

BEHAVIOUR (each item needs a test)
1. THE HEADLINE: with an unstaged edit in package.json (add a devDependency in the working tree, stage nothing but an unrelated source file) a hooked commit records the version bump and does NOT record the devDependency. After the commit, the working tree still has the devDependency and shows the new version, and `git status` still reports package.json as modified.
2. Staged edits to package.json ARE committed, together with the version bump, unchanged in every other respect.
3. Formatting and key order elsewhere in the working-tree package.json survive the hook byte-for-byte apart from the version value. Use a package.json with non-default formatting (4-space indent, or a trailing comment-free but unusual key order) to prove it.
4. The version written to the index and the version written to the working tree are the same string.
5. The existing package-json-mode tests still pass. The self-healing-after---no-verify behaviour is unchanged.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS (required, and reported)
For item 1 and item 3: break the implementation (revert to reading the working tree; parse-and-restringify the file), watch each test fail, restore, report the failure messages.

title: stageFiles/updateLockfile must fail loudly, not console.warn
description:
CRITICAL RULE 6 VIOLATION ("failure is not empty"), demonstrated by a test already on this branch: a stub npm that exits 1 — proven to have been invoked, via a marker file — leaves the commit SUCCEEDING with no signal at all. The same shape is in stageFiles(), which catches everything and only console.warn()s.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE SPECIFICALLY. If `git add` fails and the failure is swallowed, package.json is rewritten on disk but never staged: the commit records the OLD version while the working tree shows the NEW one. Every later computation counts from the wrong anchor, and the mistake is invisible because nothing is red. This is the reassuring-direction failure the rule is about.

THE CONTRACT (epic design D10)
- A failed stage aborts the commit: non-zero exit from the hook, and a message that NAMES the exact command that failed and its stderr. A blocked commit is strictly better than a commit that records the wrong version, and `--no-verify` already self-heals on the next hooked commit by design.
- No catch block in this path may return a value that is also a legal success value. Where a helper can fail, its return type carries the failure as a distinct member (string | null, a result union) and the caller must handle it.
- console.warn() is not error handling. Anything that is genuinely advisory and genuinely safe to ignore must say so in a comment stating why the commit is still correct if it fails.

IN SCOPE
- stageFiles() in src/script-manager.ts and its caller in the pre-commit path.
- The pre-commit handler's top-level error handling: a thrown error becomes a non-zero exit with a readable message, not a stack trace and not a silent success.
- Any other swallow-and-continue in the pre-commit path found while reading it; list each one you found and what you did about it.

DEPENDENCY: do 70i.5 (drop updateLockfile) FIRST. It deletes the package-manager subprocess, which is one of the two swallowed failures, so this bead then only has to harden staging and the handler's own error path.

OUT OF SCOPE
- The post-* hooks' deliberate --no-fail behaviour in dynamic-file mode. Those exist so a version-generation hiccup never blocks a checkout, and main's nonFatalSuffix was kept for exactly that reason. Do not make them fatal.
acceptance_criteria:
GATE. `bun run signal` clean. `bun test` with no failure main does not also have (baseline in the epic notes); npm_config_cache redirected into $TMPDIR; new integration tests carry a per-test timeout of at least 20000ms.

BEHAVIOUR (each item needs a test)
1. When staging the version change fails, the commit does NOT happen: git exits non-zero, HEAD is unmoved, and stderr names the failed command. Induce the failure for real rather than by mocking the whole function — for example make .git/index unwritable for the duration, or put a failing `git` earlier on PATH for the hook's subprocess. If no honest induction can be found, say so plainly in the bead notes and in your report rather than faking one.
2. After that failed commit the repository is not left in a half-updated state that would produce a WRONG version on the next attempt: either the working tree version change is rolled back, or the next hooked commit recomputes correctly from the index. Whichever you choose, state it in the bead and pin it with a test.
3. The success path is unchanged: a normal hooked commit still bumps and still exits 0.
4. Report the list of every swallow-and-continue you found in the pre-commit path and what you did about each.

NEGATIVE CONTROL (required, and reported): restore the console.warn swallow, watch test 1 fail, restore the fix, report the failure message.

title: Drop updateLockfile from the pre-commit hook (buys nothing)
description:
MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: updateLockfile() in the pre-commit path buys nothing, so it is pure cost — a package-manager subprocess on every single commit.

The probes behind that (2026-09-16):
- bun.lock records the root package NAME but not the root VERSION (grep found zero "version" keys for the root), and `bun install --frozen-lockfile` after a version-only bump exits 0.
- package-lock.json DOES record the root version, but `npm ci` after a version-only bump also exits 0.
- So no supported workflow breaks from the drift it was written to close. If closing the drift is ever wanted, `npm version X --no-git-tag-version --offline` updates both files instantly and offline — no need for this code path.

IN SCOPE
- Remove updateLockfile() and its call from the pre-commit path.
- Remove any package-manager detection, imports or helpers that exist ONLY to serve it. Check for other callers before deleting anything: detectPackageManager is also used by the husky/hook-install path, and that use must stay.
- Remove the tests that exist only to pin updateLockfile's behaviour, and keep the one that proves a hooked commit does NOT shell out to a package manager (invert the existing stub-npm marker-file test: the marker must NOT appear).

OUT OF SCOPE
- Any change to how staging failures are reported (70i.4, the very next bead, which lands on the same call site). Do 70i.5 first so 70i.4 has less surface to harden.

WHY THIS IS SAFE TO DELETE RATHER THAN DISABLE: the behaviour is recoverable from git history, no consumer can depend on a lockfile side effect of a version bump (the probes show both package managers accept the drift), and leaving it behind a flag would add a knob nobody would ever turn on.
acceptance_criteria:
GATE. `bun run signal` clean. `bun test` with no failure main does not also have (baseline in the epic notes); npm_config_cache redirected into $TMPDIR; new integration tests carry a per-test timeout of at least 20000ms.

BEHAVIOUR
1. A hooked commit in package-json mode invokes NO package manager. Proven by the inverted stub-npm test: a stub on PATH that writes a marker file is never triggered, so the marker does not exist after the commit.
2. grep shows no remaining reference to updateLockfile anywhere in src/ or tests/.
3. detectPackageManager (or whatever the husky/hook-install path uses) still works: the existing install tests pass unmodified.
4. A hooked commit still bumps package.json correctly in both calculation modes.

NEGATIVE CONTROL (required, and reported): re-add the call, watch the marker-file test fail, remove it again, report the failure message.

title: Remove stale hooks when versionMode changes
Add --mode flag so a fresh install can reach package-json mode
Handle amend/rebase/merge in package-json mode (or document as linear-only)
description:
What actually happens on merges in package-json mode, measured 2026-09-16 (not inferred). Setup each time: base 0.1.0, feature +5 hooked commits -> 0.1.5, main +1 hooked commit -> 0.1.1.

- TRUE MERGE (--no-ff), diverged main: CONFLICTS on package.json. Resolve ours (main 0.1.1) -> merge commit lands at 0.1.2. The 5 feature commits are not counted.
- SQUASH MERGE, diverged main: CONFLICTS on package.json. Resolve ours -> 0.1.2. Resolve theirs (0.1.5) -> 0.1.6.
- SQUASH MERGE, main NOT diverged: no conflict, feature version 0.1.5 carries into the index, pre-commit adds 1 -> 0.1.6.

CONCLUSION: the outcome is decided entirely by which side of the version field wins the merge resolution; the pre-commit hook then adds exactly 1 on top. A merge driver here is a POLICY choice, not a hard problem: it only has to pick a side for the version field and let normal JSON merging handle the rest of package.json.

DECIDED (Justin, 2026-09-19): OURS — the branch being merged into, i.e. main. Rationale: main's version then counts commits landed ON MAIN, monotonic and stable regardless of how people branched, and two 500-commit branches squash-merged do not produce wild jumps. A squash of a 500-commit branch lands at main+1.

IN SCOPE
- A merge driver script in the package (TypeScript, run with bun, under scripts/ or src/ — not a shell script, per the critical rules) that git invokes as `driver <ancestor> <ours> <theirs>`.
- Registration written by the install command: `package.json merge=version-manager` in .gitattributes, plus merge.version-manager.name and merge.version-manager.driver in the repo's git config. Install must be idempotent and must not clobber an existing .gitattributes.
- README documentation including the server-side caveat below, stated honestly.

IMPLEMENTATION SHAPE — do NOT write a JSON merger
The driver is invoked with %O (ancestor) %A (ours) %B (theirs) and must leave the merged result in %A. Read the version value out of %A; rewrite the version value in BOTH %O and %B to that same string; then run `git merge-file %A %O %B` and propagate its exit code. The version line is then byte-identical on all three sides so it cannot conflict, while every other key in package.json merges by git's normal line rules with normal conflict behaviour. This is a few lines and inherits git's own merge semantics instead of re-implementing them.

THE CAVEAT THAT MUST BE VERIFIED BEFORE ANY CLAIM IS MADE
A merge driver lives in LOCAL git config, so it plausibly does not run for merges performed on GitHub's servers (the merge / squash buttons on a PR). If that is true, server-side merges still conflict and still block the button, and the driver only helps people merging locally. Verify it against authoritative sources before the README says anything, and write what you find — including "not documented" if that is the honest answer.

RELATIONSHIP TO OTHER BEADS
- 70i.3 (read the index) does NOT change any outcome measured above: in both merge flows the resolved version is already staged, so reading the index yields what reading the working tree yielded.
- 70i.10 (branch suffix) makes the equal-length silent-undercount case a visible conflict. This driver then resolves that conflict by policy instead of by hand.

OUT OF SCOPE
- amend and rebase behaviour. Both are measured and recorded above and in the epic; neither is fixed here. Document them as known limitations of package-json mode rather than working around them.
design:
RECOMMENDED: merge driver that takes OURS (the branch being merged into) for the version field only, everything else normal JSON merge. Rationale: main version then counts commits landed ON MAIN, monotonic and stable regardless of how people branched; two 500-commit branches squash-merged do not produce wild jumps. Registered via .gitattributes (package.json merge=version-manager) plus a git config driver entry, both installable by the install command.

CAVEAT not yet verified: a merge driver is LOCAL git config, so it does not run for merges performed on GitHub servers (the merge/squash button). Server-side merges would still conflict and block the button. Needs checking before promising this fixes the PR workflow.
acceptance_criteria:
GATE. `bun run signal` clean. `bun test` with no failure main does not also have (baseline in the epic notes); npm_config_cache redirected into $TMPDIR; new integration tests carry a per-test timeout of at least 20000ms.

BEHAVIOUR (each item needs a test in a real fixture repo)
1. TRUE MERGE, diverged main, driver registered: package.json does NOT conflict, and the merged version is main's version (ours), not the branch's.
2. SQUASH MERGE, diverged main, driver registered: no conflict on the version field; the result follows the ours policy.
3. A genuine conflict elsewhere in package.json (both sides edit the same dependency to different values) STILL conflicts. The driver must not paper over unrelated conflicts.
4. A non-conflicting change on each side (ours adds a script, theirs adds a dependency) merges cleanly and BOTH changes survive.
5. Install registers the driver idempotently: running install twice leaves one .gitattributes entry and one git config entry, and an existing unrelated .gitattributes line survives.
6. With the driver NOT registered, the measured conflict behaviour above is unchanged — the control.

RESEARCH DELIVERABLE (blocking the README text)
A documented answer on whether GitHub's server-side merge buttons run a custom merge driver, with sources and dates, written into the bead notes. The README states the honest answer, including 'not documented' if that is what the evidence supports.

NEGATIVE CONTROL (required, and reported): unregister the driver, watch test 1 fail (the conflict returns), re-register, report the failure message.
notes:
DECIDED by Justin 2026-09-19: the merge driver takes OURS (the branch being merged into, i.e. main) for the version field. The a/b is closed; build the ours policy.

THE CAVEAT IS NOW RESOLVED — RESEARCHED 2026-09-19, and it is the bad answer.
GitHub's web merge buttons ("Merge pull request", "Squash and merge", "Rebase and merge") do NOT apply the .gitattributes `merge` attribute. Not custom `driver=` drivers, and not even the built-in `merge=union` / `merge=binary` strategies that need no external command. A PR whose package.json versions diverge is therefore still reported as CONFLICTING and its merge buttons are still blocked, exactly as today, even with the driver installed and working perfectly for the same merge run locally.

Evidence, weighted:
- STRUCTURAL AND DOCUMENTED for custom drivers: git's own gitattributes manual says a custom driver needs BOTH a versioned .gitattributes line AND a `merge.<name>.driver` entry in .git/config or ~/.gitconfig. The second never travels with the repo, so there is nowhere for a repository to ship the command. GitHub could not run it even in principle. High confidence.
- EMPIRICAL, NOT DOCUMENTED, for the built-ins: no structural barrier exists for merge=union, yet it does not work either. GitHub community discussion 9288 is a still-open feature request specifically about merge=union. kubernetes/kubernetes PR 70576 (opened 2018-11-02) is titled "gitattributes: remove the union merge driver since GitHub doesn't support it" — a major project removing the attribute because of this. Consistent reports 2013 through 2026, no counter-reports, no changelog announcing support. High confidence in the behaviour, medium in the reason.
- GitHub's own "Resolving a merge conflict on GitHub" doc never mentions .gitattributes at all. Merge queue offers only merge/rebase/squash; rulesets govern whether a merge may happen, never how content is combined.
- GitHub does honour .gitattributes for OTHER purposes (the linguist-* attributes are documented), so "GitHub ignores .gitattributes" would be too broad a statement. The gap is specific to the merge attribute during PR-merge computation.
- The only way to get custom merge behaviour server side is to stop using the button: a GitHub Actions job or a merge bot checks out both branches on a runner, sets merge.<name>.driver in the runner's real git config, runs a real `git merge`, and pushes. That works because a runner is a normal VM with real git, not because GitHub supports drivers. Out of scope here.

WHAT THAT MEANS FOR THIS BEAD. The driver is still worth building — it fixes every LOCAL merge and squash, which is how these small repos are actually merged, and it is a handful of lines. But it must not be sold as fixing the PR workflow. The README must say plainly that merging through GitHub's buttons will still conflict on package.json and must be resolved by hand or merged locally. If the PR-button case ever becomes the thing that matters, the answer is a different mechanism (an Actions-driven merge), not a better driver.

IMPLEMENTATION SHAPE (do not write a JSON merger). A git merge driver is invoked with %O (ancestor) %A (ours) %B (theirs) and must leave the result in %A. Read the version value out of %A, rewrite the version value in BOTH %O and %B to that same string, then run `git merge-file %A %O %B` and propagate its exit code. The version line is then byte-identical on all three sides so it cannot conflict, and every other key in package.json merges by git's normal rules with normal conflict behaviour.
